real_defects.issue: parseList was not idempotent: it trimmed before the 120-character cut (an option cut just after a space kept a trailing space), stripped only one leading bullet ('- - Water'), and cut by UTF-16 unit (half an emoji). The respondent's page parses the shared link again, so its listId differed from the creator's and the creator's 'combine' refused every respondent code as 'for a different list'. Reproduced with decodeList(encodeList(...)) giving a different listId.
